title: Torsion en cohomologie cristalline : notes manuscrites (s.d.), copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from §8.5 and neighbouring pages): k is a perfect field of characteristic p. X ⊂ P^r_k is smooth projective of dimension n. Y runs over the smooth hypersurface sections of X of degree d, parametrised by the open set U_d of the space of degree-d hypersurfaces. E(Y) is the 'vanishing' (évanescente) part of the crystalline cohomology H^{n-1}(Y/W), and E(Y,O_Y) is its coherent analogue inside H^{n-1}(Y,O_Y). The subscript ss means the Frobenius-bijective (semisimple, unit-root) part. By Artin–Schreier theory such a part is (étale F_p-cohomology of Ȳ) ⊗ k, so it defines a local system of F_p-vector spaces on U_d. The exact sequence (8.5.9) of local systems, induced by the sequences (8.5.1), shows the following. The local system attached to (E(Y)⊗_W k)_ss contains a sub-system that is essentially trivial: it comes from H^{n-1}(X), hence from the base, and is geometrically constant. Beyond that it has a 'genuinely vanishing' component E(Y,O_Y)_ss. (The struck-out first version said this component was Coim φ = Im φ, where φ is the map of 8.5.)

Grothendieck expects this component to give a very non-trivial F_p-representation V of G = π1(U_d). Alternatively one can use Gal(k(s)^sep/k(s)) at the generic point s of the space of hypersurfaces, but then the Frobenius elements are lost. He asks two questions:
- A marginal note asks, for n ≥ 2, whether V is irreducible.
- Is the monodromy image of G all of Aut(V) = GL(V)? Under some condition; a margin note excludes a trivially treatable case, X = P^{r-1}.

Consequence if the answer is yes and dim V ≥ 2:
- dim V ≥ 2 should hold for d large, since dim V → ∞ with d (cf. 8.5.8).
- Then every element of F_p is the trace of some element of G acting on V.
- The 'Woods Hole formula' gives #Y(k') ≡ Σ(-1)^i Tr(F | H^i(Y,O_Y)) mod p. Only the Frobenius-bijective parts contribute, i.e. traces on étale F_p-cohomology.
- Chebotarev density over the finite field k then deduces: for every nonempty open U of the hypersurface space (d large), some s ∈ U(k') over a finite extension k' gives a section Y with #Y(k') congruent mod p to any prescribed element of F_p.

Grothendieck notes that, even with Katz's help, this seems unproved even for plane curves of large degree (X = P^2). A deleted, boxed sentence said the result would already settle affirmatively the conjecture of n°6 on the 'level' (niveau) of vanishing cohomology.
errors: The Chebotarev step needs the GEOMETRIC monodromy (image of π1 of U ⊗ k̄) to be all of GL(V). It also needs control of the coset in which Frobenius elements of degree [k':k] lie, and of the constant contribution of H^*(X) (which depends on k'). This is harmless if the geometric image is GL(V), since then the traces cover F_p and absorb the constant shift, but it is not stated.

dim V ≥ 2 for large d requires the vanishing part to have growing p-rank, i.e. that general sections are 'ordinary enough'. This was later supplied for general complete intersections by Illusie/Deligne (generic ordinarity, 1990). At the time it was only a hope ('sans doute').
A minor point: for dim V = 1 the traces miss 0, so dim V ≥ 2 is indeed needed. The argument is otherwise sound modulo the monodromy hypothesis.

ideas.what: The unit-root / Frobenius-semisimple part of the vanishing coherent cohomology of hypersurface sections, viewed as an étale F_p-local system on the parameter space U_d (a p-adic, wild analogue of Picard–Lefschetz vanishing cohomology).
ideas.modern_name: unit-root F-crystal / étale p-adic local system of a family; mod-p monodromy of the p-rank (étale) part
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz (p-adic properties of modular forms / Travaux de Dwork, 1973), Deligne–Katz, Crew
ideas.where_published: Ideas of unit-root crystals appear in Grothendieck's letters and in Katz's work; not this formulation, as far as I know

ideas.what: Question whether the monodromy of π1(U_d) on the vanishing unit-root F_p-local system is irreducible and in fact equal to GL(V).
ideas.modern_name: big p-adic monodromy for p-rank strata / families in characteristic p
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ekedahl (1987, Jacobians of the universal curve), Achter–Pries (2007, p-rank strata of M_g), Chai (Hecke orbits)

ideas.what: Using the mod-p Woods Hole trace formula (#Y(F_q) ≡ Σ(-1)^i Tr(F|H^i(Y,O)) mod p) plus Chebotarev to convert big mod-p monodromy into the statement that point counts mod p of hypersurface sections in any open set take all residues.
ideas.modern_name: equidistribution of point counts mod p / Hasse–Witt traces via monodromy and Chebotarev
ideas.usually_credited_to: Monodromy-plus-Chebotarev method: Katz–Sarnak style (ℓ-adic); p-adic versions: Achter, Cais–Ellenberg–Zureick-Brown (random p-torsion of plane-curve Jacobians)
ideas.where_published: The mod-p trace formula appears in SGA 4½ / SGA 5 contexts ('formule de Woods Hole'); the application here does not, as far as I know

ideas.what: Expectation that dim V → ∞ with d, i.e. that general hypersurface sections have large p-rank in the vanishing part.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne / Illusie ('Ordinarité des intersections complètes générales', 1990)

missed.claim: An explicit conjecture/program (late 1960s): the étale F_p-local system given by the Frobenius-bijective part of vanishing H^{n-1}(Y,O_Y) over the space of smooth degree-d hypersurface sections should have irreducible, indeed full GL(V), monodromy. Consequently, the number of points mod p of hypersurface sections (e.g. plane curves of large degree) in any nonempty open set should hit every residue class.
missed.quote: l'image du groupe fondamental G dans Aut(V) ... est-elle égale à Aut(V) tout entier ? ... trouver un point s de U ... définissant une section Y telle que card Y(k') soit congru mod p à un élément de F_p donné à l'avance
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates by roughly 20–40 years the p-adic monodromy theorems of Ekedahl and Achter–Pries and the random-Dieudonné-module heuristics of Cais–Ellenberg–Zureick-Brown for plane curves. Whether full GL monodromy on the vanishing unit-root part of large-degree hypersurfaces in arbitrary X is proved in this generality is unclear to me. The question as posed (any X, any open U, Woods Hole + Chebotarev) may still be partly open, and its origin with Grothendieck is not recorded.

missed.claim: A link between the mod-p monodromy of unit-root vanishing cohomology and the 'level of vanishing cohomology' conjecture of n°6 of the same notes, i.e. torsion in crystalline cohomology and Hodge level. The link is struck out but stated: the point-count result would imply that conjecture.
missed.quote: Ce résultat ... impliquerait déjà une réponse affirmative à la conjecture du nº6 sur le niveau de la cohomologie évanescente
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests using p-adic monodromy/equidistribution to control torsion and Hodge-level phenomena in crystalline cohomology. That route is not standard in the literature on crystalline torsion.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a clearly formulated, unpublished big p-adic monodromy question for vanishing unit-root cohomology of hypersurface families in characteristic p. It is combined with the Woods Hole mod-p trace formula and Chebotarev into a concrete equidistribution statement for point counts mod p, with Katz consulted. This prefigures later work (Ekedahl, Achter–Pries, Illusie's generic ordinarity, CEZB) and is not credited to Grothendieck. It is a conjectural program, not a proof, and specialists know analogous ideas.
